lesson: A residential electrical layout is a rule check first and a modelling task second; most failures came from content (template families built for commercial work) and from Revit dialogs outside the script's reach.
rule: 1) Lay out devices in 2D first, on top of the framing layout (ARPL-ASM-0007), and check them against NEC 210.52 (wall spacing 1.83 m, counter 600 mm, bath basin 900 mm, front/back exterior, HVAC service receptacle 7.5 m) before modelling; the owner confirms. 2) Check what content exists; author missing families from Family Templates with PowerBalanced connectors (ARPL-CON-0001); wall-mounted ones from 'Electrical Fixture.rft' (switch category if needed), not from 'Lighting Fixture.rft'. 3) Place wall devices on host-wall side faces, fetching fresh face references for every placement (FP18); ceiling devices on a horizontal reference plane at the finished ceiling. 4) Before circuiting, probe the panel's supply connector (voltage, poles) against the distribution system; template commercial panelboards are 208 V 3-pole. Probe device loads (some types carry 0 VA). 5) Create circuits in the order of the planned numbering; for loads above 80 % of the default 20 A rating expect a modal warning during ElectricalSystem.Create (FP17): watch the screen, or create them with a temporary small load. 6) Place the panel schedule, export the sheet as an image and look at it; sync after the checks pass. 7) Before rough-in, check every device against the framing: wall box centre ≥ 19 + half box width + 3 mm from a stud axis (47 mm single-gang, 75 mm round 4 in), ceiling device ≥ 19 + radius + 10 mm from a rafter axis and inside its room; move the device, then re-run the NEC spacing check. 8) Model the rough-in as members of the prefab assemblies (boxes, cut-outs, sleeves, nipples) and clash-check them: only insulation, sheathing, siding and drywall may be cut, never framing. Partition walls built on site get no rough-in pieces. 9) Re-run the wall-space check whenever doors or windows change: fixed panels of sliding glass doors count as wall space and the operable panels are doorways, so posts between standard sliders usually need their own receptacle. A wall panel rebuild deletes the rough-in in that assembly; re-run it for that wall only.
validation: NEC 210.52 spacing checks pass on the 2D layout
Every device placed within 2 mm of its face (report distance)
Panel connector voltage/poles match the distribution system
Circuit numbers equal the planned numbers; ratings and loads read back
Panel schedule and sheet exported and inspected
Rough-in clash check: only soft layers cut (XPS, plywood, siding, drywall, batt)
Wall-space check re-run after every opening change
